newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA SHOULD END ROBSON ERA WITH ANOTHER CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA SHOULD END ROBSON ERA WITH ANOTHER CUP.

text.p: Barcelona start the Spanish Cup final at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium on Saturday (Kickoff 1900 GMT) as overwhelming favourites to win the trophy for the 23rd time in their history and end Bobby Robson's spell as coach in style.

By contrast, their opponents Real Betis are looking to win the cup for only the second time -- 20 years after their previous win, an 11-9 penalty shootout victory over Athletic Bilbao after the teams fought to a 2-2 draw.

If they are to defy the pundits, Betis will have to overcome a Catalan team that looks stronger on paper in almost every department and one that has already lifted the European Cup Winners Cup and the Spanish Super Cup this season, as well as finishing second to Real in the League.

The one consolation for Betis is that they are assured of a place in the European Cup Winners Cup themselves next season. Barcelona won't be defending their trophy as they are joining champions Real Madrid in the expanded European Cup.
Barcelona's team on Saturday will be composed almost entirely of international players including three Portuguese stars: goalkeeper Vitor Baia, defender Fernando Couto and striker Luis Figo.

Abdelardo Fernandez, Luis Enrique and Sergi Barjuan are all mainstays of the Spanish national team's current World Cup campaign and emphasises that the Barcelona side has not been assembled solely from expensive foreign imports.
Only at the front is there a doubt about Barcelona's abilities.

Brazilian striker Ronaldo is otherwise detained at the Copa America -- and although the Barcelona management have said he could be recalled for the final that is now unlikely. In any case there is a doubt whether he would be available to play with all the confusion over the legality of his four billion peseta ($27.5 million) move to Italian club Internazionale.
Barcelona have a number of capable midfield players like the prodigious Ivan de la Pena, who is still only 21, but nobody who comes close to the goal scoring abilities of Ronaldo.
Despite their role as underdogs, Betis are far from devoid of talent after finishing an impressive fourth in the Spanish League this season.
They were rebuilt at the start of the season with more than three billion pesetas ($25 million) spent in the transfer market.
Among the purchases was the Nigerian international and former Ajax player Finidi George, who quickly became a firm favourite with the Betis fans his thrilling runs down the right wing.
Betis will also benefit from some local knowledge about the Santiago Bernabeu stadium from arguably the best of coach Lorenzo Serra Ferrer's five major buys.
Striker Alfonso Perez is a former Real Madrid fan and player, discarded by the League champions last summer following a loan spell with Betis.
Since arriving in Seville he has gone on to set scoring records at Betis with 25 goals in the league last season, the second best tally behind Ronaldo.
Nothing would make him happier than a good display on his old home ground.
One factor in Betis's favour is that they nothing to lose.
No one other than their die hard fans expect them to win.

Even Barcelona coach Robson, who is set to be replaced by Dutchman Louis van Gaal despite the possibility of bringing three trophies to Barca this season, acknowledges that the pressure is on his side. "There's no doubt that we are the favourites."
The statistics reinforce this belief as Barcelona have already beaten Betis twice in the league this season, 4-2 in Seville and 3-0 at Camp Nou.
But if Betis are looking for any omens in their favour then there is only one.
